subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` be a non-consuming verification operation for every cron schedule, with only internal timer and on-exit watcher paths allowed to mutate scheduler counters, timing, disable state, and `deleteAfterRun` one-shots?
rationale: The branch’s technical boundary is coherent, but it deliberately changes observable manual-run semantics for existing operator and in-process callers; that compatibility policy requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
options.body: Confirm the proposed operator semantics, then require final-head real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve legacy consuming manual runs
options.body: Reject or redesign the behavior change if manual force runs are intended to consume one-shots and scheduler state.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
recommendation.body: Confirm the proposed operator semantics, then require final-head real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cron scheduling work owns the adjacent pending-slot and recomputation invariants affected by this policy choice.
